prompt: We need a CloudFormation template that creates a private AWS AppSync GraphQL API named "SuperCoolAPI" with AWS IAM authentication, introspection disabled, and a query depth limit of 10 with a resolver count limit of 100, along with a tag key "graphqlapi:createdBy" set to "SAM" and an owner contact of "blah-blah"; the API must log all field logs to CloudWatch using a dedicated IAM role that trusts the AppSync service and has the AWS managed policy "AWSAppSyncPushToCloudWatchLogs" attached, and the schema should define a type Book with a field bookName of type String and a Query type with a getBook resolver that takes a bookName argument and returns a Book.

We need a CloudFormation template that creates a Step Functions state machine named "Calculator-StateMachine" implementing a simple calculator that accepts an input JSON with an operator field (add, subtract, multiply, or divide) and an operands array of two numbers, then routes execution to a single Node.js 20.x Lambda function (named "Calculator" with 128 MB memory, 4-second timeout, and inline code performing the corresponding arithmetic operation) via a Choice state, with a default Fail state for unknown operators; the Lambda function must have an IAM role that allows it to create log streams and put log events in CloudWatch Logs, while the Step Functions state machine must have its own IAM role that allows it to invoke any Lambda function (lambda:InvokeFunction on all resources), and a CloudWatch Logs log group for the Lambda function must be created with a retention period of 3 days; finally, the template should output a sample input value: {"operator": "add", "operands": [1,2]}.

We need a CloudFormation template that creates an EC2 Image Builder pipeline to automatically build and distribute a custom AMI based on the CIS Level 1 hardened Amazon Linux 2023 ARM image, with modifications to ensure compatibility with AWS Elastic Beanstalk, and includes a lifecycle policy to delete images after a configurable number of months. The template should accept parameters for the AWS Organization ID (default "o-69lcdj4kro"), image version (default "0.0.0"), EBS volume size in GB (default 50, range 8-500), and image lifecycle in months (default 6, range 1-60). It must create an IAM role with the managed policies AmazonSSMManagedInstanceCore and EC2InstanceProfileForImageBuilder, an instance profile, and a separate lifecycle execution role with the EC2ImageBuilderLifecycleExecutionPolicy. The image recipe should use the parent image ARN for the CIS hardened Amazon Linux 2023 ARM image, set the working directory to "/root", and include a custom component that runs bash commands to add the xray user, configure rsyslog and journald for logging, adjust SSH settings (idle timeout, max sessions, PAM), set a random root password, enforce password aging (warning 7 days, min 1, max 365, inactive 30), remove an unowned directory, and pre-create the webapp user and group (UID/GID 900) with nologin shell. The pipeline should be scheduled daily, have image scanning enabled, and image tests enabled with a 720-minute timeout. The distribution configuration should distribute the AMI only in the current region, tag it with the stack name, and grant launch permissions to the specified AWS Organization (using the organization ID parameter) and to two specific AWS accounts: 449435941126 (Synapse dev) and 325565585839 (Synapse prod). Finally, a lifecycle policy should be enabled to delete AMI images after the specified number of months, selecting resources by the recipe name and version.

We need a CloudFormation template that creates a VPC with a CIDR block of 172.31.0.0/16, along with two public subnets (172.31.1.0/24 in us-east-1a and 172.31.3.0/24 in us-east-1b) and two private subnets (172.31.2.0/24 in us-east-1a and 172.31.4.0/24 in us-east-1b), where public subnets have auto-assign public IP enabled and private subnets do not; the template should also provision an Internet Gateway attached to the VPC, a NAT Gateway placed in the first public subnet with an associated Elastic IP (domain vpc), separate public and private route tables for each subnet with default routes (0.0.0.0/0) pointing to the Internet Gateway for public subnets and to the NAT Gateway for private subnets, and proper subnet-to-route-table associations; all resources must be tagged with a key "ResourceType" set to "ReInvent2020-SecurityTheWellArchitectedWay-Pattern3" and appropriate Name tags; finally, the stack should export the VPC ID and the IDs of all four subnets using the stack name as a prefix, and also output the stack name itself.

We need a CloudFormation template that creates an Amazon VPC IP Address Manager (IPAM) to centrally manage and allocate IP addresses across our AWS environment, including the necessary service-linked role for IPAM, a top-level IPAM pool with a provisioned CIDR of 10.0.0.0/9, and a Resource Access Manager (RAM) resource share to allow cross-account sharing of the IPAM pool with specified principals. The template should accept parameters for the principals to associate with the IPAM (defaulting to an empty string), the provisioned CIDR (defaulting to 10.0.0.0/9), the environment (defaulting to production with allowed values of production, test, and development), and custom tagging with a tag key defaulting to "createdby" and a tag value defaulting to "aws-cloudformation-templates". The IPAM must be created in the current region, with a private default scope, and the pool should use IPv4 addressing with a default allocation netmask length of 24, auto-import enabled, and allocation resource tags matching the custom tag key and value. The RAM resource share must not allow external principals, use the permission ARN arn:aws:ram::aws:permission/AWSRAMDefaultPermissionsIpamPool, and include the IPAM pool's ARN as a resource, with all resources tagged with the environment and custom tag key-value pairs. The service-linked role for IPAM must be created first to ensure the IPAM resource can be provisioned successfully.

We need a CloudFormation template that creates the core secrets and IAM roles for the WealthWise application’s ECS deployment, intended for a production environment. The template should generate four secrets in AWS Secrets Manager: a JWT signing secret named wealthwise/jwt-secret with a 64-character alphanumeric password excluding punctuation, a JWT refresh token signing secret named wealthwise/jwt-refresh-secret with the same generation rules, a MongoDB/DocumentDB connection string secret named wealthwise/mongodb-uri with the literal placeholder value 'REPLACE_WITH_DOCUMENTDB_CONNECTION_STRING', and a NextAuth.js session encryption secret named wealthwise/nextauth-secret also generated with a 64-character alphanumeric string. All secrets must be tagged with the environment name parameter (defaulting to production). Additionally, the template must create an ECS task execution role named with the environment prefix and suffix -wealthwise-ecs-execution, which trusts the ecs-tasks.amazonaws.com service principal, attaches the AWS managed policy AmazonECSTaskExecutionRolePolicy, and includes a custom inline policy granting secretsmanager:GetSecretValue on all four secrets. A separate ECS task role named with the environment prefix and suffix -wealthwise-ecs-task, also trusting ecs-tasks.amazonaws.com, must include an inline policy allowing ssmmessages:CreateControlChannel, ssmmessages:CreateDataChannel, ssmmessages:OpenControlChannel, and ssmmessages:OpenDataChannel on all resources to support ECS Exec. The template should output the ARN of each secret and export the execution role ARN and task role ARN using the environment name as a prefix for the export names.

We need a CloudFormation template that creates five AWS Lambda functions for contract testing of the AWSSamples::LambdaFunctionInvoker::Hook, each with an IAM execution role and corresponding CloudWatch log groups, where the functions are named using a prefix "LambdaFunctionInvokerHookTest" from a mapping with suffixes 1 through 5, each function has a configurable environment variable USE_CALLBACKS to toggle between standard and callback-based workflows controlled by five separate parameters (LambdaFunction1UseCallbacks through LambdaFunction5UseCallbacks) that accept "yes" or "no" with a default of "no", the Lambda runtime is Python 3.12 with handler index.lambda_handler, 256 MB memory, and 15-second timeout, and the inline code logic checks for an "InvalidPropertyKey" in resource properties to return a non-compliant status and if callbacks are enabled returns an in-progress status with a callback context, the IAM role uses the AWSLambdaBasicExecutionRole managed policy and is named with the prefix and the region, each Lambda function has a pre-created log group with configurable retention days (default 7) from the LogRetention parameter, all resources are tagged with Name, AppName ("AWSSamples::LambdaFunctionInvoker::Hook"), and Env ("dev"), and the template should output the five Lambda function names.

We need a CloudFormation template that creates an SNS topic subscription for multiple endpoint types—email, SQS queue, Lambda function, and HTTPS—based on user-supplied parameters, with each subscription conditionally created only if the corresponding input is provided and differs from its default placeholder. The template must accept an SNS topic ARN (defaulting to arn:aws:sns:us-east-1:123456789012:sns-topic-name) and four optional endpoints: an email address (default example@example.com), an SQS queue ARN (default arn:aws:sqs:us-east-1:123456789012:sqs-queue-name), a Lambda function ARN (default arn:aws:lambda:us-east-1:123456789012:function:sqs-queue-name), and an HTTPS URL (default https://example.com). All parameters must have strict validation patterns for ARNs, email format, and URL scheme, with length constraints and descriptive constraint messages. For the HTTPS subscription specifically, apply a custom delivery policy with exponential backoff, a maximum of 20 retries, a minimum delay target of 10 seconds, a maximum delay target of 30 seconds, 3 retries at the minimum delay, 17 at the maximum delay, and no delays for the first 0 retries. The template should expose each subscription’s ARN as an output (conditionally, matching the respective subscription creation). Additionally, include metadata such as version 1.0.0, owner Subhamay Bhattacharyya, and project name “Nested Stack Templates Collection,” along with an interface that groups parameters into SNS configuration and subscriptions sections with clear labels.

We need a CloudFormation template that creates a demonstration environment for building and using custom Python Lambda layers, leveraging a pre-existing custom resource called LayerBuilder that is imported from another stack via cross-stack references. The template must define several Lambda layers using the Custom::LayerBuilder resource type, each with a ServiceToken obtained by importing the value with the key "cfn:lambdalayer-x86-64:${AWS::Region}:arn" for x86_64 architecture and "cfn:lambdalayer-arm64:${AWS::Region}:arn" for arm64 architecture. Specifically, create an empty layer named "test-gracefull-exit" with no requirements or inline code; a layer named "boto3-latest" that includes the boto3 package; a layer named "requests-latest" that includes the requests package; a layer named "pydantic-latest" that includes the pydantic package, noting that pydantic has a compiled pydantic-core dependency so the builder's architecture must match the consumer function's architecture (x86_64 builder for x86_64 consumer); a layer named "inline-code-only" that contains no pip packages but includes a file named "eratosthenes.py" with base64-encoded Python code implementing the Sieve of Eratosthenes algorithm; a layer named "inline-code-and-requirements" that includes the python-whois package and a file named "module.py" with base64-encoded code that imports whois and defines an examine function; and an arm64 variant of the boto3 layer named "boto3-latest-arm64" using the arm64 ServiceToken import so that C extensions are built natively for Graviton consumer functions. Additionally, create an IAM role named LambdaExecutionRole that allows the Lambda service to assume it and grants permissions to create log groups, log streams, and put log events in CloudWatch Logs. Finally, create a Lambda function named DemoLambdaFuntion (note the intentional typo) with runtime python3.14, a 60-second timeout, and an inline code handler that imports boto3, pydantic, requests, the examine function from lambdalayer.module, and the sieve function from lambdalayer.eratosthenes, then prints their versions and test outputs. The function must be attached to the LambdaExecutionRole and include all five layers: Boto3LambdaLayer, RequestsLambdaLayer, PydanticLambdaLayer, InlineCodeWithPipPackageLambdaLayer, and InlineCodeLambdaLayer.

We need a CloudFormation template that creates a comprehensive set of saved CloudWatch Logs Insights queries for analyzing Claude Code usage metrics, designed to appear in the Logs Insights console for on-demand analysis of token consumption, request patterns, user behavior, cost attribution, and cache efficiency. The template should accept a parameter for the metrics log group name with a default value of "/aws/claude-code/metrics", and all queries must be associated with this log group. The solution should include real-time monitoring queries that track tokens per minute and requests per minute by user and model, a query showing current TPM/RPM as a 5-minute average, and a rate limit risk analysis query that identifies the top 100 highest token and request consumers per minute. For user analytics, include queries that analyze user sessions by aggregating token usage, API calls, session start and end times, and models used per session, an hourly activity timeline breaking down tokens, requests, and unique users by token type and model, and an errors and throttling events query that filters for error patterns, throttling, 429 status codes, rate limits, exceptions, and failures while parsing user email, error message, status code, and model fields. For cost and attribution, include queries that sum total tokens by user, by model and token type, and by organization. For debugging and analysis, include queries that calculate model efficiency metrics including total, average, minimum, and maximum tokens per request by model and token type, cache hit rate analysis by user and model that computes cache hits versus cache misses and the percentage of cache hits, cache hit rate over time on an hourly basis, cache hits by session, cache misses by session, peak usage windows in 15-minute intervals showing window tokens, requests, and active users, a session deep dive query that filters for a placeholder session ID "SESSION_ID_HERE" and displays all relevant fields chronologically, a metric field explorer that parses and displays all available fields including user email, user ID, session ID, organization, model, token type, terminal type, OTel library, and token count, and a daily usage summary query showing total tokens and requests per day for the last 30 days. The template must also include an output that provides a formatted list of all saved queries organized by category and a direct URL to the CloudWatch Logs Insights console using the AWS region where the stack is deployed.

We need a CloudFormation template that creates a Cognito User Pool named StudyBuddyUserPool with email auto-verification and a default verification message "Welcome to StudyBuddy! Your code is {####}" with subject "Welcome to StudyBuddy", requiring email, given_name, and family_name as schema attributes (all mutable and required) and using email as the username attribute, and also sets up Lambda triggers for post-authentication, post-confirmation, and pre-sign-up using the function names auth_hook and signup_hook in the same account and region; it should create a User Pool Client for the frontend named StudyBuddyFrontend that depends on the Google identity provider, allowing OAuth flows of code and implicit with scopes email, openid, and profile, callback URL at https://www.somethingcode.com/callback and logout URL at https://www.somethingcode.com/logout, with a default redirect URI pointing to the same callback, a 30-day refresh token validity, and the client secret generated; it must also deploy a custom domain for the Hosted UI using the domain signin.somethingcode.com with an ACM certificate validated via DNS, and integrate Google as an identity provider by pulling the client ID and client secret from SecretsManager using the default key paths "idp-google-client-credentials:SecretString:client-id" and "idp-google-client-credentials:SecretString:client-secret" respectively, mapping the email, given_name, and family_name attributes; finally, the stack should output the hosted sign-in domain, the user pool ARN, ID, client ID, and the callback URL.

We need a CloudFormation template that creates an ECS task definition using Fargate launch type with CPU set to 256 and memory 512, running a single container named DefaultContainer that pulls its image from the ECR repository at 1234567890.dkr.ecr.<region>.amazonaws.com/your-ecr-repo-name:latest-d195bc4919540c304d368e3082c0a6103a3661c189ba1b4863162a31ecf4b8e3, using the awsvpc network mode and a family name of mystackdevTaskDef141959DC; the task should have a dedicated task role and an execution role, both with the necessary trust policies to allow ECS tasks to assume them, and the execution role must be attached to a policy granting permissions for ECR actions including BatchCheckLayerAvailability, GetDownloadUrlForLayer, BatchGetImage on the specific repository, as well as GetAuthorizationToken on all resources, and the final output should expose the full image URI using the pattern 1234567890.dkr.ecr.${AWS::Region}.${AWS::URLSuffix}/your-ecr-repo-name:latest-d195bc4919540c304d368e3082c0a6103a3661c189ba1b4863162a31ecf4b8e3.

We need a CloudFormation template that creates a private REST API Gateway in a VPC, intended to ingest commands from an App Runner service, using the application name "shopify" and environment "development" as defaults. The template must first deploy a VPC endpoint of type Interface for the execute-api service, with private DNS enabled, attached to the VPC, private subnets (app-private-subnet-a and app-private-subnet-b), and security group (app-sg) imported from a separate stack using the naming convention `${AWS::Region}-${AppName}:vpc`, `${AWS::Region}-${AppName}:app-private-subnet-a`, etc. The API Gateway itself must be configured as a private endpoint, referencing that VPC endpoint, with a resource policy that allows invoke from any principal but denies invoke unless the request originates from the specific VPC endpoint. It must include a Cognito user pool authorizer of type COGNITO_USER_POOLS, using the imported Cognito user pool ARN (exported as `${AWS::Region}-${AppName}:cognito-userpool-arn`), with the identity source set to the Authorization header. A proxy resource with path `{proxy+}` should be created, and a method of ANY HTTP method must be integrated as AWS_PROXY, forwarding requests to a Lambda function whose ARN is imported from `${AWS::Region}-${AppName}:lambda-api-function-arn`, using POST as the integration HTTP method. An IAM role named "ApiGatewayLogPublishingRole" must be created with the AmazonAPIGatewayPushToCloudWatchLogs managed policy, allowing the API Gateway service to assume it, and this role must be associated via an AWS::ApiGateway::Account resource. A deployment must be created, depending on the method, and a stage named after the Environment parameter (e.g., "development") must be configured with caching disabled, detailed logging at INFO level, metrics enabled, data trace enabled, throttling rate limit of 10000 requests per second and burst limit of 5000, and an access log setting that writes to a CloudWatch log group named `/${AppName}/apigateway/access-log` with a retention of 7 days, using a JSON format that captures requestId, source IP, caller, user, requestTime, eventType, routeKey, status, and connectionId. Finally, a Lambda permission must grant the API Gateway service invoke access on the imported Lambda function, scoped to the API's resource path. The template should output the service endpoint URL as `https://${ApiGatewayRestApi}.execute-api.${AWS::Region}.${AWS::URLSuffix}` and export it as `${AWS::Region}-${AppName}:api-gateway-endpoint`.

We need a CloudFormation template that creates a secure, production-ready Terraform S3 state backend, including an S3 bucket for storing state files, a DynamoDB table for state locking, a KMS key for encryption, an IAM role for managing state, and a CloudTrail trail for auditing data events, all designed to avoid the chicken-and-egg problem of needing Terraform to create its own backend. The template should accept a customizable Name parameter that defaults to "terraform-state-AWS_ACCOUNT_ID" for the bucket, table, and role names, and allow configuration of lifecycle rules with a NoncurrentVersionExpirationInDays defaulting to 90 days for purging old state versions. For the logging trail, it must create a separate S3 bucket with configurable LogsArchiveInDays of 30 days to move logs to Glacier and LogsDeleteInDays of 365 days for deletion, with an optional ObjectLockEnabled feature that locks log objects for 30 days in GOVERNANCE mode when LogsObjectLockInDays is set to a non-zero value. The template should include a CloudWatch Logs group (enabled by default via the LogsGroup parameter) for state changes, with a dedicated IAM role for CloudTrail to write logs, and both the log group and trail role should be conditionally created only when LogsGroup is set to Enabled. The KMS key must have key rotation enabled and a policy that allows the root account full management, restricts encrypt/decrypt operations to only via S3 and DynamoDB services, permits CloudTrail to generate data keys, and allows CloudWatch Logs to use the key for encryption. The S3 state bucket must be private, enforce server-side encryption with the KMS key, block all public access, enable versioning, and have a bucket policy that denies PutObject requests that do not use the specific KMS key, and optionally restricts all S3 actions to requests originating from a specific VPC when the StateVpcId parameter is provided. The DynamoDB lock table should use pay-per-request billing, have a single attribute LockID of type String as the hash key, enable point-in-time recovery, contributor insights, and server-side encryption using the KMS key. The IAM role must allow the ExecutionPrincipal (defaulting to the root account) to assume it, with an optional condition requiring the principal to have a tag "Repository" with a value containing the Repository parameter when ExecutionConditionTag is Enabled, and similarly allow the AdminPrincipal to assume the role with an optional tag condition when AdminConditionTag is Enabled, and also support an SSOPermissionSet parameter to allow any role matching the AWSReservedSSO pattern to assume the role. The role should be tagged with the Repository tag and have a policy granting ListBucket and GetObject/PutObject on the state bucket, GetItem/PutItem/DeleteItem on the lock table, and DescribeKey/Encrypt/Decrypt/ReEncrypt/GenerateDataKey actions on the KMS key. The CloudTrail trail must log all data events for the state bucket, use the KMS key for encryption, write to the trail bucket, and optionally send logs to the CloudWatch log group. The template should output the KMS key alias and ID, lock table name, log group name, region, role ARN, and state bucket name.

We need a CloudFormation template that creates an RDS Proxy for an Aurora PostgreSQL cluster, intended to manage database connections securely and efficiently for a serverless application. The template should accept parameters for the application name, defaulting to "shopify", and the proxy name, defaulting to "aurora-cluster". It must create an IAM role named "ProxyDbSecretsAccessRole" that allows the RDS service to assume it, and attach a custom managed policy called "DbSecretsManagerManagedPolicy" that grants the secretsmanager:GetSecretValue action on a secret imported from another stack using the format "${AWS::Region}-${AppName}:db-secrets". Two security groups are required: one named "AuroraProxySecurityGroup" and another named "LambdaApiSecurityGroup", both associated with a VPC imported via the key "${AWS::Region}-${AppName}:vpc", with appropriate tags for the application name. An ingress rule must allow TCP traffic on port 5432 from the Lambda API security group to the Aurora proxy security group. The RDS Proxy resource itself should be named using the proxy parameter, use the POSTGRESQL engine family, enable debug logging, set an idle client timeout of 120 seconds, require TLS, and reference the IAM role ARN. Its authentication must use the SECRETS scheme with the same imported secret ARN and require IAM authentication. The proxy must be deployed across two private subnets imported as "${AWS::Region}-${AppName}:db-private-subnet-a" and "${AWS::Region}-${AppName}:db-private-subnet-b", and include both the Aurora proxy security group and an imported database security group from the key "${AWS::Region}-${AppName}:db-sg". A default target group for the proxy must associate it with the Aurora cluster imported via "${AWS::Region}-${AppName}:aurora-cluster", and configure connection pooling with MaxConnectionsPercent set to 100, MaxIdleConnectionsPercent set to 50, and ConnectionBorrowTimeout set to 120 seconds. Finally, the template should export the proxy endpoint, proxy ARN, Aurora proxy security group ID, and Lambda API security group ID using the naming convention "${AWS::Region}-${AppName}:aurora-proxy-endpoint", "${AWS::Region}-${AppName}:aurora-proxy-arn", "${AWS::Region}-${AppName}:aurora-proxy-sg", and "${AWS::Region}-${AppName}:lambda-api-sg" respectively.

We need a CloudFormation template that creates an S3 bucket for uploading images, which triggers a Lambda function on every new object creation to start an AWS Step Functions state machine. The state machine invokes a Rekognition Lambda function that analyzes the image with a minimum confidence of 75% and checks for the labels "Human" or "Person"; if detected, it passes to another Lambda that sends an SMS notification via Amazon SNS to a phone number provided as a parameter (defaulting to +14070000000). The bucket’s event notification requires a Lambda permission that is deliberately scoped to any S3 bucket in the account (arn:aws:s3:::* ) to avoid a circular dependency between bucket creation and the permission. The template includes IAM roles and policies: a shared role for the Rekognition and notification Lambdas with permissions for Rekognition (Detect*, Get*, List*, Describe*), SNS (Publish, Get*, List*), S3 (Get*, List*), and CloudWatch Logs; a separate role for the initial trigger

We need a CloudFormation template that creates an AWS Lambda function with an inline ZipFile containing Python code that retrieves a database username from an SSM parameter and prints it, along with a least-privilege IAM role that allows the Lambda function to assume the role and grants only the ssm:GetParameter action on that specific parameter, and an SSM parameter named dbUsername of type String with a default value of alice (which users can override when creating the stack, but the value must match the allowed pattern of lowercase alphanumeric characters between 5 and 12 characters). The Lambda function should use the python3.8 runtime with the handler set to index.lambda_handler, and the IAM role must have a trust policy that allows the lambda.amazonaws.com service to assume it, with a policy that restricts the resource to the exact SSM parameter using the partition, region, and account ID. The template must include a parameter for the database username with the same allowed pattern and default, and automatically pass that parameter value to the SSM parameter.

We need a CloudFormation template that creates an AWS Glue database, a Glue crawler, and an IAM role to enable automated cataloging of CloudTrail logs stored in an S3 bucket named `kk-admin` under the path `s3://kk-admin/cloud-trail/AWSLogs/`. The database name should be dynamically generated as `{stack-name}-kk-admin-db`, and the crawler name should be `{stack-name}-crawler`, with a table prefix of `cloudtrail_`. The crawler must target the specified S3 location and be configured with a schema change policy that updates the database schema in place and logs deletions. The IAM role, named `{stack-name}-role`, should assume the `glue.amazonaws.com` service principal, be attached to the AWS managed policy `AWSGlueServiceRole`, and include an inline policy granting `s3:GetObject`, `s3:PutObject`, and `s3:ListBucket` permissions on the `kk-admin` bucket and its contents. The template should output the Glue database name, crawler name, and role ARN for easy reference.

We need a CloudFormation template that creates an AWS Elemental MediaPackage channel, along with optional HLS and DASH origin endpoints, and optionally a VOD workflow with a packaging group, packaging configurations, and assets, based on the provided S3 bucket names. The template should accept parameters for the archive bucket (for live-to-VOD), the manifest name (defaulting to "index"), the output type (choose from APPLE_HLS, ISO_DASH, or ALL, defaulting to APPLE_HLS), startover window in seconds (default 0), segment duration in seconds (default 3), and a VOD source bucket (if provided, the VOD workflow is created). Additional parameters include a logical name prefix (default "MediaPackage"), environment (default "production"), and custom tags (default key "createdby" and value "aws-cloudformation-templates"). The template must create an IAM role for MediaPackage to assume, with policies granting read access to the VOD source bucket (if provided), write access to the archive bucket (if provided), and full access to SecretsManager for secrets retrieval and role pass/read. The MediaPackage channel is always created. For HLS and DASH endpoints, conditionally create them based on the output type: if the output type is APPLE_HLS or ALL, create an HLS endpoint; if ISO_DASH or ALL, create a DASH endpoint. The origination for endpoints should be DENY if a live-to-VOD archive bucket is provided, otherwise ALLOW. For VOD workflows, if a VOD source bucket is provided, create a packaging group, and conditionally create HLS and DASH packaging configurations and assets based on the output type. The role name should follow the pattern {LogicalName}-MediaPackage-{Region}. Outputs should include the channel ID, the HLS endpoint URL (if created), the DASH endpoint URL (if created), and the manifest name. All resources should be tagged with the environment and custom tag key-value pair.

We need a CloudFormation template that creates the shared IAM roles and instance profiles required by all Amazon EKS Quick Start stacks in an AWS account, designed to support the deployment and management of EKS clusters, node groups, Fargate profiles, and associated networking resources. The template must create Lambda execution roles for various operational tasks, including a CopyZipsRole that allows Lambda to read objects from any S3 bucket, a GenerateClusterNameRole for cluster naming logic, a ResourceReaderRole with ReadOnlyAccess, a CreateVpcRoleRole that can create and attach policies to a role named CloudFormation-Kubernetes-VPC, a DeleteBucketContentsRole for cleanup operations, and a CloudFormationVPCRoleCreationRole with similar VPC role creation permissions. The template must also include a ControlPlaneRole for the EKS control plane that assumes the AmazonEKSClusterPolicy, AmazonEKSServicePolicy, and AmazonEKSVPCResourceController managed policies plus EC2 describe permissions, a CleanupLoadBalancersRole with permissions to describe and delete application, network, and classic load balancers along with associated network interfaces and security groups, a CleanupSecurityGroupDependenciesRole for removing security group dependencies, a CleanupLambdasRole that can list and delete Lambda functions, a GetCallerArnRole with CloudFormation stack describe and CloudTrail lookup permissions, a RegisterTypeRole for registering CloudFormation resource types with permissions for STS, CloudFormation type registration, IAM role and policy management, S3 object reads, and SSM parameter operations, a NodeSGRole with EKS DescribeNodeGroup permissions, a FargateExecutionRole that can be assumed by eks-fargate-pods.amazonaws.com with the AmazonEKSFargatePodExecutionRolePolicy, a FargateProfileRole for creating and managing Fargate profiles with EC2 subnet describe and IAM pass role permissions, and a QuickStartParameterResolverRole with SSM parameter read access restricted to the /quickstart/amazon-eks/ path. The template must also create two EC2 instance profiles, one for unmanaged node groups and one for managed node groups, each referencing corresponding IAM roles that can be assumed by EC2 instances and include the AmazonSSMManagedInstanceCore, AmazonEKSWorkerNodePolicy, AmazonEKS_CNI_Policy, AmazonEC2ContainerRegistryReadOnly, CloudWatchAgentServerPolicy, AmazonEBSCSIDriverPolicy, and AmazonElasticContainerRegistryPublicReadOnly managed policies, with the public ECR policy only included when the partition is aws, plus a custom inline policy allowing cloudformation:SignalResource. All Lambda roles must assume the AWSLambdaBasicExecutionRole managed policy, and all roles must be named with the eks-quickstart prefix as specified. The template must use a condition to check if the AWS partition is aws for the conditional inclusion of the public ECR policy, and all IAM policies should follow least-privilege principles with resource-level restrictions where appropriate, such as limiting S3 get object permissions to any bucket, restricting IAM role creation to the specific CloudFormation-Kubernetes-VPC role, and scoping SSM parameter access to the quickstart path.

We need a CloudFormation template that creates an ECS task definition for a containerized application, along with the necessary IAM roles and logging infrastructure to support it. The template should include a parameter for the ECR repository name with a default value of "book-app", which will be used as the family name for the task definition and as a prefix for the log stream. Both roles should be assumable by the ecs-tasks.amazonaws.com service principal and should have names prefixed with the CloudFormation stack name followed by "-TaskRole" and "-TaskExecutionRole" respectively. The task definition itself should use the Fargate launch type with the awsvpc network mode, allocate 256 CPU units and 512 MB of memory, and define a single container using the public nginx image from public.ecr.aws/nginx/nginx, mapping container port 80, with the container not running in privileged mode. The container should have logging configured to send logs to a CloudWatch log group using the awslogs driver, with the log group named "/ecs/book-app" (or more precisely, "/ecs/" followed by the ECR repository name parameter value), set to retain logs for 7 days, and the log stream prefix should match the ECR repository name. The log group should be deleted when the stack is deleted. The template should export the task definition ARN, task role ARN, and task execution role ARN as outputs with names suffixed by "-task-def", "-task-role", and "-task-execution-role" respectively, all prefixed with the stack name, so that other stacks can reference these resources.

We need a CloudFormation template that creates an Amazon Security Lake data lake in the current account, ingesting logs from AWS CloudTrail management events, Lambda execution logs, Amazon EKS audit logs, Route 53 resolver query logs, Security Hub findings, and VPC Flow Logs, all using source version 2.0, and optionally sets up an S3 subscriber for a SIEM tool in a separate audit account if an audit account ID is provided; the template must create an IAM role named using a custom prefix (defaulting to "SecurityLake") followed by "-SecurityLake-" and the region, with the path "/service-role/" and the managed policy "AmazonSecurityLakeMetastoreManager", and the data lake itself should reference that role as the metastore manager; the subscriber, when created, should grant S3 access to the principal identified by the provided audit account ID using the external ID "SIEM", subscribe to all six log sources, and be named "Audit" with a description including the stack name; additionally, a subscriber notification with SQS configuration should be attached to that subscriber; all resources should be tagged with an "environment" tag (defaulting to "production") and a custom tag key-value pair (defaulting to key "createdby" and value "aws-cloudformation-templates"); the template should accept parameters for the audit account ID (optional, default empty), the logical name prefix (default "SecurityLake"), the environment (production/test/development), and the custom tag key and value (both required, with default values as above).

We need a CloudFormation template that creates a custom SSM Document of type Command to inventory specific running processes on EC2 instances, along with an SSM Association that applies this document to all instances on a scheduled basis, using default process keywords for Linux (CassandraDaemon, dse cassandra, mysql, postgres, redis-server, redis-sentinel, memcached) and Windows (sqlservr, cassandra, mysql, postgres, redis-server, redis-sentinel, memcached) with a schedule expression defaulting to "rate(30 days)", and exporting the document reference as a stack output for cross-stack consumption.

We need a CloudFormation template that creates a CodeBuild project in the us-west-2 region, using account 043490748814, to replicate three CodeCommit repositories—card-service, rule-service, and ecs-pipeline—from us-west-2 to ap-northeast-2 by mirroring their contents whenever a commit is pushed to the mainline branch. We need a CloudFormation template that creates a VPC with a configurable number of public subnets across different Availability Zones, using CIDR 192.168.0.0/16 with DNS support and hostnames enabled, and accepting a parameter called SubnetCount with allowed values of 1, 2, or 3 (defaulting to 1) that determines how many public subnets to create, each using a /24 CIDR block: 192.168.1.0/24 for the first, 192.168.2.0/24 for the second, and 192.168.3.0/24 for the third, placed in the first three Availability Zones of the region respectively, and tagged with Name (stack name hyphen subnet number), Application (stack name), and Network (Public); the template should conditionally create the second and third subnets only when SubnetCount is 2 or 3 and exactly 3 respectively, attach an internet gateway to the VPC, create a public route table with a default route (0.0.0.0/0) to the internet gateway, and associate that route table with each created subnet; finally, the template should output the VPC ID, the first subnet ID as MainSubnetId, and a comma-separated list of all public subnet IDs as SubnetIds that conditionally includes only the subnets that were actually created based on the SubnetCount parameter.

We need a CloudFormation template that creates a Cognito-based authentication infrastructure for Kibana users, including a user pool named "KibanaUsers" that allows only admin-created users with email as both the username attribute and auto-verified attribute, enforcing a minimum password length of 8 characters and requiring the email schema attribute to be mutable and required, along with an identity pool named "KibanaIDPool" that allows unauthenticated identities, an IAM managed policy granting full ES HTTP access to all resources, an IAM role that uses a web identity trust policy with the identity pool as the audience and the authenticated condition, and a role attachment linking the authenticated role to the identity pool, with the outputs exporting the user pool ID, user pool ARN, and identity pool ID using the stack name as a prefix.

We need a CloudFormation template that creates a comprehensive set of CloudWatch metric filters, alarms, and CloudWatch Logs query definitions to monitor an AWS account against the CIS AWS Foundations Benchmark, specifically covering sections 3.1 through 3.14, all tied to a single CloudTrail log group. For each of the 14 CIS controls, you must create a CloudWatch Logs metric filter that parses the log group for specific patterns, a corresponding CloudWatch alarm that triggers when the sum of that metric over a 300-second period (except for the KMS key alarm which uses a 60-second period) is greater than or equal to a threshold of 1, with missing data treated as not breaching, and a CloudWatch Logs query definition that provides a pre-built query for investigating the events. The specific controls to implement are: 3.1 for unauthorized API calls filtering on error codes '*UnauthorizedOperation' or 'AccessDenied*'; 3.2 for console sign-ins without MFA filtering on 'ConsoleLogin' events where 'MFAUsed' is not 'Yes'; 3.1 and 3.3 combined for root account usage filtering on user identity type 'Root' where 'invokedBy' does not exist and the event type is not 'AwsServiceEvent'; 3.4 for IAM policy changes filtering on a comprehensive list of 16 IAM event names like DeleteGroupPolicy, PutRolePolicy, and AttachUserPolicy; 3.5 for CloudTrail configuration changes filtering on CreateTrail, UpdateTrail, DeleteTrail, StartLogging, and StopLogging; 3.6 for console authentication failures filtering on 'ConsoleLogin' events with an error message of 'Failed authentication'; 3.7 for disabling or scheduled deletion of customer-created CMKs filtering on events from 'kms.amazonaws.com' with event names 'DisableKey' or 'ScheduleKeyDeletion'; 3.8 for S3 bucket policy changes filtering on events from 's3.amazonaws.com' with event names like PutBucketAcl, PutBucketPolicy, and DeleteBucketPolicy; 3.9 for AWS Config configuration changes filtering on events from 'config.amazonaws.com' with event names StopConfigurationRecorder, DeleteDeliveryChannel, PutDeliveryChannel, and PutConfigurationRecorder; 3.10 for security group changes filtering on event names like AuthorizeSecurityGroupIngress, CreateSecurityGroup, and DeleteSecurityGroup; 3.11 for NACL changes filtering on event names like CreateNetworkAcl, DeleteNetworkAclEntry, and ReplaceNetworkAclAssociation; 3.12 for network gateway changes filtering on event names like CreateCustomerGateway, AttachInternetGateway, and DetachInternetGateway; 3.13 for route table changes filtering on event names like CreateRoute, ReplaceRouteTableAssociation, and DeleteRoute; and 3.14 for VPC changes filtering on event names like CreateVpc, ModifyVpcAttribute, and AcceptVpcPeeringConnection. All alarms must send their notifications to the referenced SNS topic ARN, and the template should include the necessary DependsOn clauses to ensure the alarms are created in the correct order, specifically the RootAccountLoginsAlarm depends on the NoMfaConsoleLoginsAlarm, the FailedConsoleLoginsAlarm depends on the RootAccountLoginsAlarm, and the DisabledOrDeletedCmksAlarm depends on the FailedConsoleLoginsAlarm.

We need a CloudFormation template that creates an EC2 Image Builder pipeline to produce both x86 and ARM64 Amazon Linux 2023 golden AMIs pre-configured with Docker, Docker Compose, Git, Python 3, and the Synapse client with pandas and pysftp dependencies, intended for use by a research team that requires a standardized, publicly shareable base image. We need a CloudFormation template that creates a SageMaker data quality monitoring job definition to automatically assess the quality of data being sent to a deployed machine learning endpoint, ensuring that any data drift or anomalies are detected in near real-time. The template must first create an IAM role named MySageMakerRole that allows the SageMaker service to assume the role, and this role will be referenced by the job definition. The data quality job definition itself should be named MyDataQualityJob and must use a custom container image located at 123456789012.dkr.ecr.us-west-2.amazonaws.com/my-image:latest for the monitoring application. The job should take its input from an existing SageMaker endpoint named my-endpoint, with the data being written to a local path of /opt/ml/processing/input. For output, the job must write monitoring results to an S3 bucket at s3://my-sagemaker-bucket/output using a continuous upload mode, with the local output path set to /opt/ml/processing/output, and both the S3 output and the processing volume must be encrypted using existing KMS keys: the output should use the key with ARN arn:aws:kms:us-west-2:123456789012:key/my-existing-kms-key-id, and the processing volume should use the key with ARN arn:aws:kms:us-west-2:123456789012:key/my-existing-volume-kms-key-id. The compute resources for the job should consist of a single ml.m5.xlarge instance with a 20 GB volume, and the job should have a maximum runtime of 3600 seconds.

We need a CloudFormation template that creates a CodeBuild project for building and deploying a custom CloudFormation resource provider for PostgreSQL user management, along with its associated IAM role and CloudWatch log group. We need a CloudFormation template that creates a set of Amazon Athena named queries to analyze Amazon AppStream 2.0 usage reports data, all targeting a database named "appstream-usage" which contains tables named "sessions" and "applications". The template should include twelve specific named queries: one for average session length per stack for the current month and one for the previous month, each computing the average session duration rounded up to the nearest minute and hour; daily session counts for the current and previous month; all sessions for the current and previous month; streaming hours per user for the current and previous month, with each session duration rounded up to the nearest hour; users per application for the current month; and users per application for the previous month, the latter two joining the applications and sessions tables on user_session_id and filtering by year, month, and day conditions to cover the previous month and the first five days of the current month. All queries should be named with the prefix "AS2_" and appropriate suffixes, with descriptions summarizing their purpose, and must be scoped to the "appstream-usage" database.
